title: Admit one interior colon in a decision tag so contract:<name> is writable
action:
Per D2 (plan.md, Approach, S2): the locked label is the tag convention contract:<name> over the active decision set. That tag cannot be written today - tag_pattern_test (verbs/decisions/scanners.rs:476-483) enforces /^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/ and normalize_tags (:498) refuses anything else. This cell makes the locked spelling writable and nothing more; it adds no contract semantics, no query, no guard. Those are later slices.

Step 1 - widen the predicate. tag_pattern_test must accept AT MOST ONE interior colon: the segment before it and the segment after it each still match the current rule (start with [a-z0-9], continue with [a-z0-9-]). Accept 'cells' and 'contract:cells'. Refuse ':cells', 'cells:', 'contract::cells', 'contract:cells:extra', and anything the current predicate already refuses (uppercase, underscore, dot, space, empty). Keep the change inside tag_pattern_test - do not restructure normalize_tags or normalize_tag_event_tags_value; both call the predicate and both must inherit the widening for free. There are exactly three call sites repo-wide: scanners.rs:498, verbs_write.rs:271, and the test at tests.rs:1528.

Step 2 - TAG_PATTERN_DISPLAY (scanners.rs:474) is the string every refusal message prints. Change it in the same commit so it describes the predicate you just wrote. A refusal that quotes the old pattern while the code accepts a colon is a lie to the user, and it is the single most likely defect in this cell.

Step 3 - tests, beside the existing tag tests in verbs/decisions/tests.rs (start from the call site at tests.rs:1528 and the tests around it; judge existing coverage first and author only the gap). From plan.md's risk map, cover: one interior colon accepted; a plain no-colon slug still accepted (the regression that matters); two colons refused; a leading colon refused; a trailing colon refused; and a table of tags that already exist in this repo's decision store - at minimum cells, contract, slp, orchestration, advisor, cli, ci - still validating. Do NOT read the live .bee/decisions.jsonl from a test; carry the representative tags as a literal table. Add one test asserting TAG_PATTERN_DISPLAY and the predicate agree: every string the display pattern describes as legal is accepted, and the sample illegal ones are refused.

Step 4 - the taxonomy is not a second obstacle and must not become one. classify_decision_tags (scanners.rs:581) appends any unknown tag to docs/decisions/taxonomy.json candidates and only refuses an EMPTY tag list, so a contract:<name> tag will be recorded as a candidate rather than refused. Verify that by reading the function; change nothing there. Note in the spec sync (step 5) that the checked-in taxonomy will grow one candidate per contract name.

Step 5 - sync docs/knowledge/areas/decision-memory/overview.md: state the tag slug rule as it now stands, including the single-interior-colon namespace form and what it is for (contract:<name>, the derived contract-status label of D1/D2), plus the taxonomy-candidate side effect from step 4. Keep it to a short paragraph; do not restate the whole decision store.
